newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-Hart wary of big men in Springbok pack.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-Hart wary of big men in Springbok pack.

text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, July 7 - South Africa were reverting to their traditional strengths in rugby by re-introducing big men to their test team, All Black coach John Hart said.
Hart and his team head to Johannesburg on Wednesday for their first Tri-series clash of the season at Ellis Park on July 19, NZPA reports.
After watching the Springboks-British Lions test series, won by the Lions 2-1, on television, Hart said he thought the smaller, more mobile men were missing from the Springboks scrum.

"I think South Africa is going back to what had been their strength, to their history, their heritage -- strong physical approach in the forwards -- and it's quite fearsome. Very hard to combat really."

However, the musclemen in the All Black frontline were already looking forward to an unfinished business at Ellis Park no sooner had they consigned the first of their three Bledisloe Cup trans-Tasman rugby test to the archives.
"We know it'll be tough as always but we love to meet the South Africans," prop Olo Brown said.
Brown was part of the All Black pack that ground down the Australians at Lancaster Park on Saturday to take a 1-0 lead in the three cup matches.
The next two clashes in Melbourne and Dunedin will double up as the Tri-series matches.
"I think it's in everybody's mind," the 100kg, 1.85m front rower, regarded as the best tighthead prop in the business, said of the All Blacks' two consecutive losses at Ellis Park.
Of three All Black matches at the magnificent rugby venue, the All Blacks have won one and lost two.
The 27-24 1992 victory in the new South Africa test in 1992 -- the Springboks re-introduction to international competition after years of isolation -- was under coach Laurie Mains.
Brown, Sean Fitzpatrick and Richard Loe were the front trio then.
The All Blacks lost the 1995 World Cup final there and last year's last dead-rubber test.
"We haven't got fond memories of the place, maybe we can change that this time -- that's out challenge," Brown said.
All Black coach John Hart said the clash with South Africa, who won the third test against the Lions yesterday, was a major target for his players.
"Sean (Fitzpatrick) is already excited about it," Hart added.
"We'll get excited. It's a head-on challenge for us, we'll take, we'll give it all we've got."
